text:
Alex Ovechkin set another record this week: his assist on Boone Jenner's goal was the 763rd of his career, passing Nicklas Backstrom for the most in Capitals history, as Tom Gulitti of NHL.com noted. The same week, CBS Sports wrote that he is struggling to contribute and Defector called him a tough watch. Both things are true, and both say something about a 41-year-old with more than 900 career goals.

He has 1 goal and 5 assists in 20 games, playing 13.6 minutes a night. He hasn't scored in 15 games.

Here is the case for patience: those 15 games produced 4.4 expected goals, the quality-of-chance measure. For the season he has 5.54 expected goals and a 2.8% shooting percentage against our range of about 10% to 15% for him. His shot is still in the 97th percentile for speed in NHL Edge tracking. We flag him as due: the chances are still there.

His skating is a different story, with his top speed at the bottom of the league. The question is whether Washington keeps feeding him chances long enough for the finishing to return.
headline: Records and a drought
